rows.what the ink shows: The cancelled opening retains a tall looped initial P-like stroke, a low horizontal body and one small raised point over the latter part. The thick cancellation coincides with both word bodies; no separate q descent or recoverable complete que sequence is distinguishable in the enlarged residual ink. The phrase therefore remains uncertain.

The beginning Il is visible as a capital I with a short top bar followed by a looped l. After it, the cancellation covers the rounded letter bodies; a tall central stem, a detached raised point and a final low loop survive, but several crossing deletion/insertion strokes merge with those joins. They do not establish the complete contient l’unité sequence. Narrow the uncertainty only by releasing Il.

After the underlined b and comma there is a short heavily darkened word group with a small upright near its left, two low humps and a downturned right tip. The middle is filled in, and neither the division into non/nul nor a separate terminal l can be distinguished. Retain the existing uncertainty.

The small inserted sign above the end of spectraux has an upper curved arm turning down into a narrow middle return and a broader lower arm; the two stacked parts make the handwritten E. Its body is clear of the cancellation on the following line.

To the right of the deleted b, a short hook, a low oval remnant and a later tall crossed stem remain between the cancellation lines. The following group survives only as low connected bumps and a rightward tail. Multiple horizontal strokes pass through both words, so their full sont dans sequence is not separable.

The short deleted insertion retains the initial pointed v with a connected rounded o turn, a detached i dot, a small open s-shaped hook and a compressed final in ending in a long low n tail. The cancellation runs along its top, leaving these lower letter forms visible.

After the formula and period, the first letter is a tall closed oval O whose bottom meets the deletion line. Beside its right edge is a separate short n with one rounded hump and a low finishing stroke. The larger curve to the right continues upward as cancellation rather than another letter.

The deleted short word beneath the end of the first proposition line has one tall initial upright and several short lower stubs. A thick horizontal cancellation fills the joining strokes, and a diagonal cancellation crosses the centre. The individual u and n shapes cannot be separated from those overlaid strokes.

Between soit and the replacement f, the deleted symbol retains a rounded loop and a long downward stem curling left at its foot. This is the visible varphi form; the adjacent f has a separate tall upper stroke and is outside this mark.

The word before borélienne has a rounded entry at the left and a small raised stroke toward the right, but its intervening letters are covered by a dense horizontal cancellation. The remaining outline does not expose the succession of letters needed to establish continue.

In the insertion after bornée, the first word is struck through so heavily that only a few detached lower fragments and an upright near the right survive; its double-p structure cannot be recovered. The following compact remains legible: an open c, connected low strokes, a downward p turn, and a high crossed terminal t before the comma. The uncertainty can therefore be confined to support.

The deleted word directly before nulle has a curved initial s, two distinct descending p loops below the cancellation line, a short low connecting segment, and a tall terminal t crossed by the deletion. Those surviving descenders and the ending identify support despite the horizontal strikeout.

At the far left of the next deleted line, a short oblique entry and several tall right-hand strokes are buried in a compact ink block. Multiple horizontal cancellations and a diagonal stroke pass through it. No distinct d-m-e-t sequence remains separable, so Admet is retained as uncertain.

After the separately assigned opening deletion, the upper canceled line begins with a small upward curl, then an angular descending return and a dot above the following low sequence. A heavy horizontal cancellation occupies the letter bodies; a low comma-like hook and several small lower curves survive farther right. These fragments do not separate the four source-placeholder words reliably.

The short word just before the tall following character retains a small low initial s, a rounded continuation below the cancellation, a detached oblique i-dot above it, and a final upright t with a short cross stroke. Those surviving letters support soit despite the line through the word.

The upper line continues with a tall narrow stem and a lower loop, followed by a low horizontal stroke; farther right is a high hooked onset, a broad bowl-like return ending in a small loop, and a comma. The cancellation intersects the ascenders and joins the remaining strokes, so the identities and word division remain unresolved.

The lower canceled line has a large open C, a low rounded connection and a conspicuous narrow tall loop near x545. The following low body is crossed through; a dot remains near x631, then two rising strokes near the right end. The tall loop makes a start such as Cela plausible, but the middle and ending are not distinguishable enough to replace the existing uncertain phrase.

The continuation on the lower line shows an initial tall stroke with an open lower loop, long low curved joins, a small upper hook around x920, and another small loop farther right. The heavy cancellation runs along the body and removes the intervening letter distinctions; no reliable three-word recovery is supported.

Between sous-algèbre and fermée, the compact abbreviation has a shallow connected initial run, then a strongly rising stroke returning in a deep narrow downstroke, and a separate raised terminal t. The raised t and compressed body support the source abbreviation uniformt; no written full ending -ément is present.
